newsitem.title: USA: Presidential debate gets lackluster TV ratings.
newsitem.headline: Presidential debate gets lackluster TV ratings.

text.p: Less than one-third of U.S. television households in 34 top markets tuned in to Sunday's presidential debate, a far smaller proportion than watched a comparable 1992 debate, Nielsen Media Research said on Monday.

The 90-minute programme featuring Republican candidate Bob Dole and President Bill Clinton, a Democrat, got a combined 31.2 rating for its broadcast on ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox, the research outfit said. Figures for CNN were not immediately available.

ABC's debate coverage drew a 10.0 rating and a 15 share; NBC got a 10.8 rating and a 16 share, CBS got an 8.5 rating and a 13 share, and Fox earned a 2.8 rating and a 4 share. For Fox, only 33 markets were surveyed.

A rating expresses the number of households tuned to a programme during the average minute expressed as a percentage of all U.S. households with a television set. A share is the percentage of households viewing a programme out of the total number of households using their television.

For an Oct. 15, 1992, debate between Clinton and then President George Bush, the combined rating in all markets was 46.3, Nielsen said. That meant that 69.9 million people watched the debate. The survey included ABC, CBS, NBC and CNN but not Fox.
By contrast, the top-rated show last week, NBC's hospital drama "ER," got a 24.2 rating and a 40 share. The lowest-rated network show, a Fox vehicle called "Big Deal," got a 3.4 rating and a 6 share.
Nielsen was not immediately able to say how many people watched Sunday's debate.
